name: type
description: Tells you HOW a command name will be interpreted: alias, builtin, function, or executable file and its path.

flags.description: Description of how the shell resolves the name.
Path only (if it is an executable file).
One-word result: alias, builtin, function, file.

examples.explanation: Your ls is an alias — this explains behavior differences between your shell and scripts.

examples.output:
echo is a shell builtin
echo is /usr/bin/echo
examples.explanation: Two echos exist: the builtin wins. Knowing this explains subtle behavior differences.
git is a real executable file, not a builtin or function.
Locates a program — a more informative which.

about: The shell resolves a name in this order: alias, function, builtin, then PATH lookup. type shows exactly which step matches, which is the first diagnostic when a command behaves differently in scripts than interactively (scripts skip aliases).
mistakes: Using which for builtins — which only searches PATH and misses aliases, functions, and builtins.
